newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly fall, mogas holds ground.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly fall, mogas holds ground.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly weaker on Monday, traders said.
Gas oil activity picked up after a very sluggish time last week. Two Russian cargoes were sold, both around high cif quotes flat to $1, a touch stronger than Friday's high cif quotes flat.
FOD heating oil was talked sharply higher at fob high quotes +$4 compared with flat to a discount heard on Friday.
"The premium has been talked up -- people want Med prices stronger to price the Indian tender while picking up material in the Middle East," said one dealer.
No trades were heard at this level.
Naphtha edged lower matching the decline in NWE prices where weaker crude futures and sluggish end-user demand weighed on the market, traders said.
Speculation surfaced that a major trader was getting ready to load a cargo out of the Med for the Far East, where prices have been steady. This was not confirmed.
"It's basically the same situation (as NWE)," a Spanish trader said. "The end-users are getting the material from the refiners."
Gasoline prices held steady and supply was still seen tigher than its NWE counterpart.
No cargoes are left for February and demand is still popping up from eastern Med destinations.
High sulphur fuel oil prices in the Med were notionally weaker on Monday in line with falling crude oil futures and sagging prices in northwest Europe.
Dealers said with cargoes in NWE valued only around $90 on a cif basis, published quotes around $100 cif Med were overdone.
Low sulphur fuel oil was weaker too. A little interest remains into an Italian refiner for early March but otherwise demand remains slack, and supply continues to pile up.
